name: Cheltenham Half Marathon
notes: The A race. Target 1:21-1:23, model predicts 1:22:23. COURSE (from a clubmate's 2025 file — her run, not his — who ran 1:21:02, so her splits map the course at almost exactly his goal pace): 101m gain over 21.09km, ~4.8m/km, rolling rather than flat, net slightly downhill start to finish. Her watch had no barometric altimeter, so treat the metres as approximate and the shape as the signal. Km 1 is downhill and her fastest of the day (3:38) — the start is a trap. Highest ground is the first 8km, which roll continuously. Flattest running is roughly 14-18km. The sting is km 19-20: a climb of about 11m that produced her slowest split of the race (4:11, seven seconds off anything else), immediately followed by a 6m drop to the line where she ran 3:54. Expect the 20km split to look bad and the last km to be free. HER PACING IS THE WARNING: first 10km 37:08 (3:43/km), second 10km 39:33 (3:57/km) — 2:25 lost in the back half after going out 7 sec/km faster than her own average. 3:43/km is Shep's current 10K race pace, so running with that early group means racing a half at 10K pace.

name: Crete 10K
notes: IN DOUBT as of 27 Sep — he says it could be off and expects to know on the 28th. Treat 4 Oct as open until confirmed. Losing it costs nothing in training terms: it was always a fun race with beers on the way over, no taper, sitting inside the HM recovery window. If it is off, see the possible 4-mile race below, which he raised as the replacement and which is a completely different proposition — a record attempt, not a jog.

name: Club 4-mile (possible)
notes: Raised 27 Sep as the replacement if Crete falls through. A home race, run for sharpness — but he flagged the club record at 23:30 (HIS FIGURE, PREFIXED 'I think' — VERIFY IT BEFORE ANY OF THIS IS USED). THE NUMBERS SAY THIS IS THE BETTER RECORD TARGET OF THE TWO, AND IT IS NOT CLOSE. Projections to 4 miles: 23:17 via the blended 5K, 23:19 via the blended 10K, 23:20 via the blended half, and 23:02 off Cheltenham alone. Three independent blended routes agreeing inside 2.5 seconds is unusually well-conditioned, and every one of them is INSIDE 23:30 — by 11 to 28 seconds. Compare Guy Fawkes: blended 29:32 against a 29:12 record, 20 seconds SHORT, with only the optimistic single-race figure (29:10) level with it. So he is inside the 4-mile record on every projection and outside the 5-mile record on all but the most generous. THE DATE DECIDES WHETHER THIS IS A GOOD IDEA. If it lands on 4 Oct as a straight swap for Crete, it is two weeks after a maximal half with NO quality work since the 12 Sep tempo — the aerobic fitness would be there and the sharpness would not, and 3:39/km off three weeks of easy running is not a record attempt, it is a disappointment. Mid-to-late October is the version that works: it then sits inside the Guy Fawkes sharpening block as both a tune-up and a record attempt, and a hard 4-mile two to three weeks out is textbook preparation for a 5-mile race rather than a conflict with it. It is also not the thing the 18 Oct XC cancellation was protecting against — that was about mud, cambers and trail shoes on an achilles, and a road 4-mile carries none of it. Ask on confirmation: the date, the surface, and whether 23:30 is right.

name: Guy Fawkes 5
notes: 5 miles, and the first race he actually races after Cheltenham. Club record 29:12. TWO PROJECTIONS, AND THE GAP BETWEEN THEM IS THE POINT: Riegel off Cheltenham alone (1:21:03) gives 29:11, level with the record. race_prediction.json, which blends four clean races including an untapered June 10K and a July 5K in 24-25C heat, gives 29:34 — 22 seconds SHORT. The blended figure is the more honest planning number; the single-race figure is what he is capable of on his best current day. Treat the record as reachable but genuinely requiring the block, not as something current fitness hands him. THE RUN-IN IS CLEAR AND DELIBERATE: he cancelled the 18 Oct XC on 20 Sep to make it so, having already dropped 31 Oct, which costs him the XC league. Nothing hard sits in the four weeks before this except Crete on 4 Oct, a fun run with beers and no taper. Those ~4 weeks after HM recovery are to be written as an actual sharpening block — short, fast work at 5-mile pace, not half-marathon volume. Do not let it drift into general aerobic work; he has paid the league for it.

name: Cross country
notes: Trail shoes, no spikes. Sits in base / early marathon build — no conflict. OPTIONAL again: the XC league needed 3 of 4 and he has now dropped both 31 Oct and 18 Oct, so the league cannot be completed and this fixture is no longer load-bearing. Run it if he fancies a hard off-road effort; skip it without cost.

name: Boddington 10
notes: Club record up for grabs at 1:01:00. Course confirmed flat, so Riegel holds without a downward adjustment. TWO PROJECTIONS: off Cheltenham alone (1:21:03) 1:00:50, ten seconds inside; off race_prediction.json's four-race blend 1:01:38, 38 seconds short. The blend is the planning number. Either way this is closer than it was in September, and it has four months of marathon base-building in front of it — the aerobic work for Manchester is exactly the work that moves a 10-mile time. Falls mid-way through that build, so it needs a short taper written into the block rather than being run off unbroken loading.

name: Cross country
notes: Trail shoes. Seven weeks out from Manchester (18 Apr), inside the marathon build. OPTIONAL again now the league is out of reach — which removes the one scheduling problem flagged for the winter: this no longer has to happen in the middle of marathon-specific work. Default to skipping it unless he says otherwise.

name: Manchester Marathon
notes: Goal sub-3 (4:16/km). Volume, not fitness, is the binding constraint, and Cheltenham widened the margin rather than closing a gap: race_prediction.json now projects 2:51:16 off four blended races (2:49 off Cheltenham alone), against 2:52 before the race. The fitness is comfortably there on paper. What is missing is that he has never run one, his longest run ever is ~29 km, and carbohydrate at marathon pace in marathon quantity is untested.
